decisions.reason: As a generic address utility with limited differentiation from larger standard tools, its market test is likely largely resolved by now and management would reallocate effort to more strategic energy-platform modules.

A niche Austrian gas-grid-fee database is close to the firm's capabilities but outside its German core and requires ongoing regulatory maintenance, so its option value is likely below its carrying cost unless demand is clearly strong.
This service fits the firm's core regulated-energy calculation know-how and platform direction, so with relatively low continuation cost it remains a worthwhile option to retain.

An end-customer tariff database leverages the firm's data assets and complements its broader market-data and compliance offerings, making it sensible to keep while it can still scale through the platform.
Custom web services are less standardized than the firm's long-run SaaS goal but they use existing capabilities, support client retention, and can still generate adjacent business at manageable risk.

A postal-code lookup service is easy to imitate and peripheral to the firm's differentiated energy-market offering, so management would likely stop marketing it and shift resources to higher-value products.
